hooks.name: TypeScript Quality Check
hooks.description: On saving a hand-written .ts/.tsx file, run the project's existing type-check and lint commands and report errors with file paths and line numbers.

action.prompt:
A TypeScript/TSX file was just saved. Run a quality check using only what the project already has configured.

1. Discover commands. Read package.json scripts (and tsconfig.json / eslint or biome config) before running anything. Do not invent commands or install tools.
   - Type-check: prefer an existing script such as "typecheck", "type-check", "tsc" or "check:types". If none exists but tsconfig.json does, run `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit`.
   - Lint: run an existing "lint" script (or eslint/biome if configured). If no lint config exists, skip lint and say so.
2. Run the type-check, then lint, once each, in non-watch mode. Use the package manager indicated by the lockfile.
3. Report results concisely. List each problem as `path:line:col - message (rule/TS code)`. If everything passes, say so in one line. If no TypeScript tooling is configured, say that and stop.
4. Read-only: do NOT edit, format, or auto-fix any file. Do not use `--fix`. Do not modify unrelated files. Offer to fix issues only if the user asks.
5. Avoid recursion: ignore generated or build output (node_modules, dist, build, out, .next, coverage, *.d.ts, *.generated.*). Do not write any files, so this check cannot retrigger itself.
